office: the Department of Civil Registration and Census

routes.label: in person at the civil registration office of one's dzongkhag: the card printed in Thimphu and received in 5 to 6 days

cards.for: a first card, or a renewal within six months of expiry

note: The Bhutanese (12 September 2015), quoting an official of the Department of Civil Registration and Census: Nu 100 for a first card and for renewing one whose expiry is six months away or less; Nu 300 for renewing earlier, or for a change of image, on production of the old card; Nu 400 for a lost card (these later cases aren't modelled). Renewal is done in one's own dzongkhag, the card printed in Thimphu reaching the dzongkhag in 5 to 6 days, and the applicant must come in person. The age at which a first card is due and the card's term aren't given, so every age is offered and the term is null; the Department's own guidelines could not be fetched (the host reset every connection).

sources.title: The Bhutanese, CID processing made more flexible for citizens (12 September 2015)
sources.said: Instead, they can now renew the CID from their own dzongkhags. ... However, people in the dzongkhags have to wait for 5 to 6 days to receive the printed CID cards from Thimphu, as the only CID printing machine is located in Thimphu. ... A person has to pay Nu 100 for fresh/processing of CID cards for the first time and Nu 100 for renewal of CID cards if the date of expiry of the earlier issued CID card is less than or equal to six months. ... If the expiry date of earlier issued CID cards has duration more than six months then the person has to pay Nu 300,
